title: Cokernel presentation of the supported constant pro-etale coefficient sheaf
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. On the small pro-etale sites with their small skeleta [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and use ordinary sheaves of $A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!$ be extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and $i_*$ the underived module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Let $\epsilon:j_!A_U\to A_X$ be the open adjunction counit, using $j^{-1}A_X=A_U$, and let $\rho:A_X\to i_*A_Z$ be the constant restriction map, whose component on a weakly etale $W\to X$ sends a constant section $a$ to the same constant on $W\times_X Z$. Then
$$j_!A_U\xrightarrow{\epsilon}A_X\xrightarrow{\rho}i_*A_Z\longrightarrow0$$
is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Equivalently $\rho$ is a cokernel of $\epsilon$ in the abelian category of ordinary module sheaves. No quasi-compactness assumption on $j$ or finiteness assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Section 9, proof of Theorem 9.4 on p. 67; Stacks Tag 095L (etale-cohomology, lemma-ses-associated-to-open) is the etale model only. Pro-etale constant-coefficient extension without quasi-compactness is agent-formulated by local lifting of locally constant functions.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] for $X$ and $Z$. The direct-image definition gives $(i_*A_Z)(V)=A_Z(V_Z)$, where $V_Z=V\times_X Z$. The specified $\rho$ is restriction of functions: restriction $C(|V|,A)\to C(|V_Z|,A)$ is a ring map natural in $V$, and it sends each constant $a$ to that same constant. The two maps from the constant presheaf therefore agree, and uniqueness for its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies them on $A_X$. Put $P=P_{A_U}$, the extension presheaf in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and denote its sheafification unit by $\eta:P\to j_!A_U$. Its canonical map $b:P\to A_X$ is the identity under the specified coefficient restriction when $V$ factors through $U$, and is zero otherwise. Its sheafified map is the counit $\epsilon$. Since $V_Z$ is empty whenever $V$ factors through $U$, $\rho b=0$; uniqueness in module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives $\rho\epsilon=0$.

source.place: Canonical maps of Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); finite-constant maps identified by the sheafification universal property.

proof.text: Let $V\to X$ be affine and $s\in A_Z(V_Z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $V_Z\hookrightarrow V$ is closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $|V|$ is quasi-compact; its closed subspace $|V_Z|$ is therefore quasi-compact. The finite-section node identifies $s$ with a continuous function to finite discrete $A$. Its nonempty fibres $C_a$ form a finite clopen partition of $|V_Z|$, and each $C_a$ is quasi-compact. For each $a$ choose an open $W_a\subset V$ with $W_a\cap V_Z=C_a$ using the subspace topology. Choose affine neighbourhoods inside $W_a$ of the points of $C_a$ and retain finitely many covering $C_a$. Do this for every $a$. Their union $O$ covers $V_Z$. The closed subset $V\setminus O$ is quasi-compact and lies in $V_U$, so finitely many affine opens contained in $V_U$ cover it. All these affine opens together cover $V$. On each member chosen inside $W_a$ the constant $a$ lifts $s$; on a member contained in $V_U$ the target has no points, so zero lifts $s$. This is a finite Zariski affine cover, hence a pro-etale cover by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the open-object localization of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. General $V$ is first covered by affine opens. Thus $\rho$ is locally surjective. No covering of $V_Z$ is lifted, and $V_U$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Agent finite-coefficient replacement for Tag 09AH: finite Zariski cover of an affine object; no application of the quasi-compact-open localization theorem.

proof.text: Let $K=\ker\rho$, computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $g\in K(V)$, the finite-section node gives a continuous function $g:|V|\to A$ vanishing on $V_Z$. Put $D=g^{-1}(A\setminus\{0\})$ and $E=g^{-1}(\{0\})$. These are disjoint clopen subsets covering $V$, and $D$ factors through $U$: it has no point over $Z$, and factorization through an open subscheme is the open-localization assertion of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Their open subschemes give a pro-etale cover, including when one is empty. On $D$, send $g|_D\in P(D)=A_U(D)$ to $\eta(g|_D)$ in $j_!A_U(D)$; on $E$ take zero. The sheaf axiom glues these uniquely because the overlap is empty. Call the resulting section $q_V(g)$. The clopen subsets pull back to the corresponding subsets for a restricted section, so uniqueness of gluing proves naturality in $V$. Addition and scalar-linearity hold after intersecting the two-piece covers of the sections in question: on a part where a section can be nonzero the object factors through $U$ and the formula is the linear map $\eta$; on the part where all input sections are zero both sides are zero. Thus $q:K\to j_!A_U$ is a module-sheaf morphism.

source.place: Agent kernel calculation for the finite constant sheaf: clopen nonzero locus and sheaf gluing, replacing the w-contractible kernel calculation in Tag 09AH.

proof.text: Write $\kappa:K\hookrightarrow A_X$ for the kernel inclusion. Step 1 factors $\epsilon$ uniquely as $\kappa h$ for $h:j_!A_U\to K$. On the cover $(D,E)$ of Step 3, $\epsilon q$ is respectively $g$ and zero, hence $\epsilon q=\kappa$. Since $\kappa$ is monic, $hq=1_K$. To prove $qh=1_{j_!A_U}$, precompose with $\eta:P\to j_!A_U$. If $V$ factors through $U$, the formula of Step 3 agrees with $\eta$ on every section of $P(V)$, checked on its nonzero and zero clopen loci. If $V$ does not factor through $U$, $P(V)=0$, so agreement is automatic. Thus $(qh)\eta=\eta$. The universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives $qh=1_{j_!A_U}$. Consequently $h$ is an isomorphism and $\epsilon$ identifies $j_!A_U$ with $\ker\rho$; in particular $\epsilon$ is monic. This argument uses no claim that a section of a sheafification already comes from a section of its presheaf.

source.place: Module-sheafification universal property applied to the explicit clopen kernel map of Step 3.

proof.text: Step 2 makes $\rho$ epic: if two module-sheaf morphisms from $i_*A_Z$ agree after $\rho$, their values on any section agree on a cover where that section lifts, hence agree by the sheaf axiom. Step 1 gives the zero composite, and Step 4 identifies its kernel with the image of $\epsilon$. By [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], this is the asserted exact sequence. In an abelian category the epic map with that kernel is its cokernel, so $\rho$ is the stated cokernel of $\epsilon$. Module-linearity follows from pointwise ring operations and the direct-image action in [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image].

source.place: Abelian-category conclusion corresponding to Tag 09AH, applied only after the finite-coefficient argument above.
